landing.definitionTitle: Gifts and surprises that arrive as a moment, not a package
landing.definition: Gifts and surprises are personal moments you create for someone else: an unexpected note, a reveal, or a keepsake they did not see coming. Online, that can be a shareable page they open on any phone—your words, a photo, and music inside a virtual love letter. The surprise is the reveal.
definitionPoints: A link they can open immediately
A reveal instead of a buried text
Optional custom music inside the gift
A keepsake they can reopen later
landing.definitionNote: Gift-giving is a long-standing social ritual for marking care and relationship. A virtual surprise keeps that ritual when you cannot hand something over in person.
landing.pickerTitle: Choose the format for your gifts and surprises
landing.pickerDescription: Love letter is live today. The other formats are on the way—use them as a preview of the surprises this studio is building around your words and music.
landing.whyTitle: Why people send gifts and surprises as a link
landing.whyDescription: A shipped object is still wonderful when you have time. When the moment is today—a birthday morning, a long-distance night, a thank-you you do not want to bury in chat—a shareable surprise is the format that can actually arrive.

whyItems.title: The surprise can happen now
whyItems.description: There is no address form, no delivery window, and no waiting for a courier. You create the page, copy the link, and the reveal can happen during a call or first thing on their birthday.

whyItems.title: The gift is made of your details
whyItems.description: A generic e-card is a template with a name dropped in. Here the message, photo, and optional song are the gift. That is what makes virtual gifts and surprises feel like they came from you.

whyItems.title: Music can live inside the reveal
whyItems.description: Add a custom song written around their story, pick a finished track from your library, or upload audio you have the right to use. The envelope opens, then the music starts.

whyItems.title: They can reopen it later
whyItems.description: Texts disappear in a thread. A virtual love letter stays on its own page, so the photo, words, and song can be opened again after the first surprise fades.

landing.occasionsTitle: Gifts and surprises for the moments that need a reveal
landing.occasionsDescription: Use a virtual love letter when the words matter as much as the object. Pair it with a custom song when you want the surprise to keep playing after they close the envelope.

occasions.title: Birthday morning
occasions.description: Send the link before they wake up. They open an envelope, see a photo, and hear a song that uses their name—then you can still follow it with a birthday song gift.

occasions.title: Anniversary and just because
occasions.description: Mark a date, or send a surprise on an ordinary Tuesday. A short letter plus one shared memory usually lands harder than a long speech.

occasions.title: Long-distance love
occasions.description: When you cannot be in the same room, a link still creates a shared second. They open the envelope while you are on the call, and the music fills the rest.

occasions.title: Thank-you and support
occasions.description: Gratitude gets lost in a chat stack. Put the specific thing they did in a letter, add a photo from that day, and let a song carry the feeling you could not fit in a text.

occasions.title: Apology and reconnection
occasions.description: A careful message deserves a quieter reveal than a notification banner. Write the words you mean, then let optional music hold the tone after they finish reading.

occasions.title: Holidays and family days
occasions.description: Mother's Day, Father's Day, Christmas morning, or a holiday you invented together. The format stays the same: your words, a photo, and music they can replay.

faq.question: What are gifts and surprises you can send online?
faq.answer: Gifts and surprises you can send online are shareable digital moments—usually a link that opens a personal page. On One Custom Song, that starts as a free virtual love letter with your message, a photo, and optional music. The recipient opens it on any phone, with no app and no account.

faq.question: Are these virtual gifts free?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating and sending a virtual love letter is free. You can write a message, add a photo, and share the link without a paywall. If you want original music inside the surprise, start a free custom song preview and attach it when you are ready.

faq.question: Do I need an account to send a surprise?
faq.answer: No. You can create a virtual love letter without signing in. An account is only needed if you want to pull a finished song from your library. Uploading a photo or creating a new custom song follows the editor flow on the next page.

faq.question: How do I share gifts and surprises after I create them?
faq.answer: You get a private link. Copy it and send it by text, WhatsApp, email, or any chat. The recipient opens the link in a browser, taps to open the envelope, and reads your message. They do not need to install an app or create an account.

faq.question: Can I add music or a custom song to the surprise?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a custom song around their story, choose a finished song from your library, or upload an audio file you have the right to use. Music is optional, but it is what makes gifts and surprises feel like more than a note.

faq.question: What occasions work for virtual gifts and surprises?
faq.answer: Birthdays, anniversaries, long-distance nights, thank-yous, apologies, and just-because moments all work. Use the love letter when you want an intimate reveal. For a longer musical gift, pair the surprise with a custom birthday or anniversary song.

faq.question: Is a virtual love letter better than a text?
faq.answer: A text is fast, but it disappears in a thread. A virtual love letter gives the same words a reveal: they open an envelope, see a photo, and can hear music. It is still instant to send, and easier to reopen later than a chat bubble.

faq.question: Can the recipient open the gift on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The gift page is built for phones. They open the link in a mobile browser, tap the envelope, and read the message. There is no app store step, no login, and no shipping address.

loveLetter.writingTitle: Letters by heart: how to start, what to write, and a template to lean on
loveLetter.writingDescription: The hardest line is the first one. Borrow an opener, steal an idea, or copy the love letter template below into the editor above — then swap in the details only you two share. An online love letter lands for the same reason a paper one does: it is specific, and it is theirs.
loveLetter.writingStartTitle: How to start a love letter
loveLetter.writingStartDescription: Open with a moment instead of a greeting. Any of these first lines works — pick the one that sounds like you:
writingStartItems: “I keep thinking about the day we ___ , and I never told you what it did to me.”
“No anniversary, no reason — I just wanted you to have something that is only yours.”
“I am bad at saying this out loud, so I wrote it down where I cannot rush it.”
“You always ___ , and I notice it every single time.”
loveLetter.writingTemplateTitle: Love letter template you can copy
loveLetter.writingTemplateDescription: Copy this structure into the message box above, or send the whole love letter online as a link with a photo and music. Fill the blanks, then delete any line that is not true:
writingTemplateLines: Dear ___ , I keep thinking about the moment we ___ .
I still remember how you ___ , and how it made me feel ___ .
What I love most is the way you ___ , even when ___ .
Thank you for ___ — I know it was not easy.
Next, I want us to ___ . Keep this letter until we do.
loveLetter.writingIdeasTitle: Ideas for a love letter when the page stays blank
loveLetter.writingIdeasDescription: Six things worth writing about, in any order. One true detail beats ten adjectives — in an online letter or on paper:
writingIdeasItems: A memory only the two of you share: the trip that went wrong, the song from that summer.
One small habit of theirs you have never thanked them for.
What changed in your life after they arrived, in one before-and-after sentence.
A promise for the next year, small enough to keep.
The thing you were too shy to say on the day it happened.
Why today, of all days, they are getting a letter.
loveLetter.writingNote: Paper or screen, the ritual is the same. An online letter only adds the reveal: they tap an envelope, see your photo, and hear the music you chose.

faq.question: Who can see my virtual love letter?
faq.answer: Only people you send the gift link to can view it. There is no public gallery. If they do not have the URL, they cannot open the letter.

faq.question: How long are virtual love letters kept?
faq.answer: Gifts stay available so they can be reopened later. Treat the link like a private keepsake: share it with the person it is for, and keep a copy in My Gifts if you are signed in.

faq.question: Where can I find all my gifts?
faq.answer: Gifts you create while signed in are saved to your personal gifts feed at My Gifts. Open that page to copy a link again, preview the shared page, or send it a second time.

faq.question: Do I need an account to send a virtual love letter?
faq.answer: No. You can write a message, add a photo, and share the link without signing in. An account is only needed if you want to pull a finished song from your library or keep the gift in My Gifts.

faq.question: Is the virtual love letter free?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating and sending a digital love letter is free. There is no ad-removal paywall on the letter itself. If you want original music inside it, start a free custom song preview and attach it when you are ready.

faq.question: Can I add a custom song to the love letter?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a custom song around their story, choose a finished song from your library, or upload an audio file you have the right to use. Music is optional.

faq.question: How do I send the virtual love letter?
faq.answer: After you create the gift, you get a private link. Copy it and send it by text, WhatsApp, email, or any chat. The recipient opens it in a browser and taps the envelope. They do not need an app or an account.

faq.question: Can they open it on a phone?
faq.answer: Yes. The gift page is built for phones. They open the link in a mobile browser, tap to open the envelope, and read your message. There is no app store step.

faq.question: How to start a love letter when you do not know what to write?
faq.answer: Start with one specific memory instead of a greeting: the day, the place, the small thing they did that stayed with you. The writing help section on this page lists ready-to-use openers, ideas for a love letter, and a fill-in-the-blank love letter template you can copy into the editor. Ten honest minutes beats a perfect paragraph.
